newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY KELER PLANS REAL-TIME CLEARING BY END-1998.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY KELER PLANS REAL-TIME CLEARING BY END-1998.

text.p: Hungary's Central Clearing and Depositary House (KELER) will publish a two-round tender next week for the supply of a money and security account management system for the real-time clearing of deals, KELER said on Wednesday.

"We would like the system to be operational by the end of 1998," Csaba Lantos, Chairman of KELER's board of director told a news conference, adding the system should also provide real-time information to the clients of KELER about their accounts.
The clearing house has already published a closed tender for the supply of another system for the clearing of option deals.

The Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) and the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) are ambitious to be the first in central and eastern Europe to introduce option products and are looking to launch the market this year.
Lantos added that KELER also planned to raise the number of daily clearing times of over-the-counter government securities deals to four from the current one, probably around the middle of the year.

He said KELER would finance the planned developments from a capital increase decided on Tuesday by the annual general meeting of the clearing house's shareholders -- the BSE, the BCE and the National Bank of Hungary.
The shareholders decided to raise the registered capital to 2.5 billion forints from 500 million forints, using the reserves, in which some 400 million forints will remain after the capital increase.
KELER posted an after-tax profit of 1.41 billion forints last year, up from 873.7 million forints in 1995.
Lantos said KELER needed developments as Hungary's securities and futures markets were expanding very rapidly.
KELER said it cleared 172,840 BSE deals in 1996, up by 243 percent from 1995, while the BSE's duplicated turnover rose to 1,145 billion forints from 253 billion forints in 1995.
The BCE's turnover rose more than fivefold in 1996 compared with 1995, to 925.8 billion forints, KELER said.
